column1: # tuluaq19-cut-parts.tsv: the Tuluaq-19's cut pieces (files of 20250107)
# Every piece in the design's own 2D cutting file, measured: the reference for
# this tool's bill of materials and panel development on an imported design.
#   Retrieved 2026-10-21. Laboratori d'envol publishes its designs and the
#   program that draws them (LEparagliding, GNU GPL) at laboratoridenvol.com.
# METHOD: the frames "for cutting table" and the internal-structure frames of
#   the 2D DXF. A piece is a closed outline at its CUT size: the seam allowance
#   (15 mm on panels and ribs, 25 mm leading edge, 10 mm trailing edge; its section 6) is part of the outline. Holes are the closed loops inside a

#   piece and are taken out. This file draws loose LINE segments; they were joined into outlines. Its diagonals carry three parabolic cut-outs each, drawn against the sewing line: counted here as holes (30, the program's "parabolic holes").
#   Each panel is also listed by itself, by its cell (in the rib column), in the
#   order the file draws them: from the centre out.
#   And each piece sewn inside the wing (section 12) by itself, added
#   2026-10-22: every full diagonal by the rib its lines hang from and the
#   side it runs to, every strap by its row and inboard rib, and every rod
#   pocket by its rib (its program's offset before 3.30), read off
#   where the program lays them out and each confirmed against the piece the
#   diagonal is as this file draws it: its whole outline (gross), and its
#   three cut-outs drawn against the sewing line (holes), the allowance
#   left whole across them — as the program drew them before 3.30.
#   One side of the wing: the whole wing is twice this, the centre rib once.
#   Units: the file's own, centimetres; areas cm2.
# CHECKS: rib 1 is gnu-A at 0.9 thickness (0.11721 c2) plus 15 mm over its contour, 8693 cm2 against 8698.67; its holes are its section 4, 2003 cm2 exact against 1993.98 as a polygon.
